title: Medieval Kingdom: The Great Siege
description: Defend your medieval kingdom against a rival warlord's siege. Command knights, archers, and wizards to protect your king, secure treasure vaults, and outmaneuver the invading army in this tactical grid battle.
learning_objectives: Understand medieval military tactics and siege warfare concepts
Learn defensive resource allocation and positioning
Practice risk assessment in high-stakes combat scenarios
Develop patience and timing in strategic engagement

core_skills.name: Combat Judgment
core_skills.description: Evaluating when to engage vs defend (prospect theory)

core_skills.name: Siege Patience
core_skills.description: Waiting for the right moment to strike vs rushing in (self-regulation)

core_skills.name: Tactical Flexibility
core_skills.description: Adapting formations to enemy movements and terrain (cognitive flexibility)

core_skills.name: Warrior Spirit
core_skills.description: Maintaining morale and effective command after losses (psychological resilience)

how_to_play: Select your kingdom's blue units to see their movement range
Green indicators show valid moves, red shows enemies in attack range
Knights charge in straight lines, Archers strike from afar, Wizards move diagonally
Use special abilities: the King can Rally troops, Wizards can Freeze enemies
Capture the enemy Warlord or accumulate 60 Gold to claim victory!
Treasure Vaults generate gold each turn — control them!
Beware of swamps (slow movement) and castle walls (impassable)!

player_pieces.label: King
player_pieces.description: Your monarch. If captured, the kingdom falls. Can rally adjacent troops for enhanced movement.

player_pieces.label: Knight
player_pieces.description: Armored cavalry that charges in cardinal directions with great speed.

player_pieces.label: Wizard
player_pieces.description: Powerful diagonal mover who can freeze enemies with arcane magic.

player_pieces.label: Soldier
player_pieces.description: Loyal infantry that moves steadily in all directions.

ai_pieces.label: Warlord
ai_pieces.description: The enemy commander. Capture them to end the siege.

ai_pieces.label: Dark Rider
ai_pieces.description: Fast enemy cavalry charging in straight lines.

ai_pieces.label: Siege Engine
ai_pieces.description: Heavy diagonal attacker with devastating siege capability.

ai_pieces.label: Raider
ai_pieces.description: Aggressive foot soldiers that advance relentlessly.

external_events.label: The Plague
external_events.narrative: A terrible plague sweeps across the battlefield! All units are weakened.

external_events.label: Allied Reinforcements
external_events.narrative: Allied forces arrive from a neighboring kingdom! Your troops gain renewed vigor.

external_events.label: Harsh Winter
external_events.narrative: A bitter winter descends! Movement across the battlefield becomes treacherous.

move_tips.capture: Every enemy captured weakens the siege. In medieval warfare, reducing the enemy's fighting strength through decisive engagements wins wars.
move_tips.resource: Securing treasure vaults funds your war effort. In medieval leadership, controlling economic resources is as important as military strength.
move_tips.objective: Holding the castle keep gives strategic advantage. In medieval warfare, fortified positions multiply your defensive capability.
move_tips.risk: Crossing swamps slows your advance but may outflank the enemy. In medieval tactics, terrain awareness separates good commanders from great ones.
move_tips.reward: Treasure chests boost your war funds. In medieval kingdoms, seizing opportunities to grow your treasury enables future military campaigns.
move_tips.center: Controlling the battlefield center gives you tactical flexibility. In medieval warfare, central positioning allows rapid redeployment to any threatened front.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Managing resources across multiple rounds to reach the best outcome
transfer_exercises.real_world: Planning study time over a semester rather than cramming before exams
transfer_exercises.challenge: Create a resource management plan for your next month: budget time/money/energy across competing priorities.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from negative events across game rounds
transfer_exercises.real_world: Maintaining performance after setbacks in a sports season or project
transfer_exercises.challenge: Track your energy/mood for 5 days. Notice patterns. What depletes you? What restores you?

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

cultural_context: Understanding history builds the contextual thinking valued in India's competitive examinations (UPSC, CBSE, ICSE). Medieval Kingdom: The Great Siege develops the analytical reading of historical events that sharpens both academic performance and civic awareness.
